fns.desc: pr_process_channels() loops `while (end-pos>2 && ch->op_classes <= op_class_count)` writing `cl = &ch->op_class[ch->op_classes]` with NO check of ch->op_classes against PR_MAX_OP_CLASSES (15, proximity_ranging.h:28). op_class_count is a raw wire byte (0-255) taken directly from an attacker-controlled Proximity Ranging Channel List (parsed from received EDCA/NTB Capability or Operation Mode attributes via pr_process_edca_capabilities/pr_process_ntb_capabilities/pr_process_op_mode, themselves reachable from pr_process_usd_elems on unauthenticated USD frames and from the PASN Auth1/2/3 wrapper path). A crafted channel list with op_class_count>15 and enough trailing bytes drives ch->op_classes past the 15-element op_class[] array bound, causing an out-of-bounds write via `cl->op_class=...`/`os_memcpy(cl->channel, pos, cl->channels)` (up to 60 attacker-controlled bytes per overrun entry) into memory beyond struct pr_channels -- a real, remotely-triggerable buffer overflow. Notably, the sibling function pr_channels_intersect()/pr_op_class_intersect() DOES bound-check both res->op_classes and res->channels against PR_MAX_OP_CLASSES/PR_MAX_OP_CLASS_CHANNELS, confirming this is an omission rather than intentional design.

pr_process_pasn_ranging_wrapper() allocates `buf = wpabuf_alloc(1000)` at :2066, then on the length-underflow guard `if (offsetof(struct ieee80211_mgmt, u.auth.variable) > len) return -1;` returns without `wpabuf_free(buf)` -- every other exit path in this function frees buf (directly or via the end: label). Currently unreachable in practice because the sole callers (pr_pasn_handle_auth_1/2) are only invoked from pr_pasn_auth_rx after it already validates `len >= offsetof(...)` at :2527, but if that invariant is ever relaxed (or a new caller added) this becomes a live leak.
